argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower certification position than the auditor attributes to the release request. It does not support clean certification without caveat, but it does support a compliant certification packet on aggregate-readiness grounds if the packet is treated as conditional on explicit disclosure of the unresolved enterprise refund-policy summarization limitation. That is consistent with the evidence showing aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, while also recognizing that the named launch slice remains below target and the draft runbook is not approved closure. The audited claim is therefore better understood as caveated certification, not unsupported clean certification.
claims_about_business_cost: No claim about business cost is needed to justify the position. The supportable path is the narrowest one: avoid escalation beyond what the record requires by treating this as caveated certification rather than forcing either unsupported clean certification or outright rejection.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against any claim of unconditional clean compliance: the unresolved limitation in a named launch use case must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance, and the current draft runbook does not satisfy that approval standard. The same policy does permit certification with explicit limitation disclosure, because disclosure is the required control when material weakness remains and approved closure is absent. The conflict in the current model-card draft should be treated as a documentation defect to be corrected in the certification packet, not as proof that certification itself is categorically noncompliant.
concessions: The current record does not support a present-tense claim that the model is cleanly certifiable without material caveat.
The draft monitoring and rollback runbook is not an approved mitigation because threshold and review date remain TBD.
The current model-card draft statement that there are no known material limitations is inconsistent with the admissible evidence and must not be relied on as-is.
The record does not include completed proof that the required disclosure has already been finalized or approved.
